statement: Define tail(i), for 0 <= i < n, as the largest j with 0 <= j < n and grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if no such j exists. Call a permutation p of {0,...,n-1} admissible if tail(p[k]) <= k for every 0 <= k < n, and let inv(p) be the number of pairs (a,b) with 0 <= a < b < n and p[a] > p[b]. The function returns a result r and either (i) there exists an admissible permutation and r is the minimum of inv(p) over all admissible permutations p, or (ii) no admissible permutation exists and r = -1. This r is exactly the minimum number of adjacent row swaps needed to make all cells above the main diagonal zero, or -1 if that is impossible.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns a result r: it does not panic, fail an array-bound check, or overflow on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, -1 <= r <= n*(n-1)/2.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Define tail(i) as the largest j with grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if no such j exists. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if there is no permutation p of {0,...,n-1} such that tail(p[k]) <= k for every 0 <= k < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if the input grid is already valid, that is, grid[i][j] = 0 for every 0 <= i < j < n.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Define tail(i) as the largest j with grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if no such j exists, and define inv(p) for a permutation p of {0,...,n-1} as the number of pairs (a,b) with 0 <= a < b < n and p[a] > p[b]. Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, there exists a permutation p of {0,...,n-1} such that tail(p[k]) <= k for every 0 <= k < n and inv(p) = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Define tail(i) as the largest j with grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if no such j exists, and define inv(p) for a permutation p of {0,...,n-1} as the number of pairs (a,b) with 0 <= a < b < n and p[a] > p[b]. Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, every permutation p of {0,...,n-1} satisfying tail(p[k]) <= k for all 0 <= k < n also satisfies inv(p) >= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Define tail(i) as the largest j with grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if no such j exists, and let t_0 <= t_1 <= ... <= t_{n-1} be the values tail(i) sorted in nondecreasing order. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if there exists k with 0 <= k < n and t_k > k.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: len(grid) = 1; grid[0] has length 1; grid[0][0] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let a = grid[0][1] and b = grid[1][1]. The function returns a result r and: if a = 0 then r = 0; if a = 1 and b = 0 then r = 1; if a = 1 and b = 1 then r = -1.
preconditions: len(grid) = 2; every row grid[i] has length 2; and every grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 2 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; every grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1; and there exist distinct row indices i,j with grid[i][n-1] = 1 and grid[j][n-1] = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on grid and rH on H, r = rH.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; every grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1. Let H be any grid satisfying the same size and binary conditions with the same n, and such that for every 0 <= i < n, the largest j with H[i][j] = 1, or -1 if none, equals the largest j with grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if none.

statement: Define tail(i) as the largest j with grid[i][j] = 1, or -1 if no such j exists. Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, r is at least the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and tail(i) > i.
preconditions: Let n = len(grid). n >= 1 and n <= 200; every row grid[i] has length n; and for every i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.
